To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
chemokines are expressed in neurons and glia in neuropathic states and that their receptors are expressed on both neurons and glia.
chemokines are involved in neuron-glia communication in neuropathic conditions.
chemokines are involved in neuron-glia communication in the spinal cord and contribute to pain signalling in neuropathics states.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of chemokines in neuropathic and inflammatory pain and how this can be used to identify potential targets for the treatment of chronic pain.
understanding how glial cells communicate with neurons and how aberrant signalling in these pathways contributes to neuropathic pain.
the identification of new therapeutic targets for the treatment of chronic pain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the chemokine CX3CL1/Fractalkine, and its receptor CX3CR1 are involved in neuropathic and inflammatory pain, and that the chemokines CCL2/MCP-1 and CCL21/SIP-1, and their receptors CCR2 and CCR7, respectively, are involved in neuropathy.
chemokine-mediated neuron-glia communication contributes to neuropathic pain and that chemokine receptor blockade is a promising approach for treating neuropathic pain.
chemokines are involved in the neuropathic pain state and that chemokine receptor agonists and antagonists are potential targets for the treatment of pain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the chemokine receptor CX3CR1 is expressed on spinal microglia and astrocytes and that the chemokines CX3CL1 and CCL21 are upregulated in the spinal cord of animals with chronic constriction injury and that the chemotaxis of spinal microglia to these chemokines is attenuated under neuropathic conditions.
chemokines and chemokine receptors are potential novel targets for treating neuropathic pain.
chemokine-mediated neuron-glia communication is a key component in neuropathic states, and thus may be a novel approach for treating neuropathic pain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
chemokines may be involved in neuron-glia communication in neuropathic states and thus represent a potential target for treating neuropathic pain.
chemokines are important mediators of neuron-glial interactions and may be a novel therapeutic target in neuropathic conditions.
chemokines are important modulators of neuron-glia interactions in the spinal cord and may contribute to the development and maintenance of neuropathic conditions.
